title: Normality descends under scalar field extension
statement: Let $F\subseteq E$ be fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension], and let $B$ be a commutative $F$-algebra (a commutative ring with a unital ring map from $F$). Form the commutative tensor-product algebra $B\otimes_F E$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(b\otimes e)(b^{\prime}\otimes e^{\prime})=bb^{\prime}\otimes ee^{\prime}$ and unit $1\otimes1$. If $B\otimes_F E$ is a normal ring, then $B$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: every prime localization of $B$ is an integrally closed domain. No finiteness, domain, nonzero, algebraicity or separability assumption is made on $B$ or on $E/F$.

source.place: Tag 033G, label lemma-descent-normal, specialized to B -> B tensor_F E. The map is faithfully flat: an F-basis of E containing 1 identifies scalar extension of any B-module with a direct sum of copies of that module.

proof.text: Put $S=B\otimes_F E$ and let $i:B\to S$ be $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], $i$ is faithfully flat, hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Fix any prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] there is a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ with $i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 033G, lemma-descent-normal, prime-lifting reduction; Tag 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings

proof.text: Write $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$ and $C=S_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], $j:A\to C$, $b/t\mapsto i(b)/i(t)$, is a flat local homomorphism of local rings. Its hypothesis is only flatness of $i$; we do not use the optional Noetherian clause. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] makes $j$ faithfully flat. By the hypothesis that $S$ is normal and [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $C$ is an integrally closed domain.

source.place: Tag 033G, lemma-descent-normal, reduction to local source and target; Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization (6); Tag 00HR, lemma-local-flat-ff

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] for $j$ and the zero ideal, $j$ is injective. Consequently $A$ is a domain: $1_A=0_A$ would give $1_C=0_C$, and $uv=0$ gives $j(u)j(v)=0$, so either $j(u)=0$ or $j(v)=0$, whence $u=0$ or $v=0$.

source.place: Tag 033G, lemma-descent-normal, sentence proving the local source is a domain; Tag 05CK, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective

proof.text: Let $x=a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, $b\ne0$, satisfy a monic equation $x^n+c_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+c_0=0$ with $c_k\in A$. The formula $u/v\mapsto j(u)/j(v)$ defines an injective ring map $\operatorname{Frac}(A)\to\operatorname{Frac}(C)$: denominators stay nonzero by injectivity of $j$, equality of fractions is cross multiplication, and a fraction maps to zero only when its numerator maps to zero. The image $y=j(a)/j(b)$ satisfies the same monic equation with coefficients $j(c_k)$, since a ring map preserves each sum and product in the equation. By integral closedness of $C$ in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], there is $s\in C$ with $y=s/1$. Cross multiplication in the domain $C$ gives $j(a)=j(b)s$.

source.place: Tag 033G, lemma-descent-normal, sentences beginning Next, suppose that a/b is integral and Then a/b in S

proof.text: The equality $j(a)=j(b)s$ means $j(a)\in (bA)C$: the ideal generated by the images of the multiples of $b$ is exactly $j(b)C$, since sums of multiples of $j(b)$ are multiples of $j(b)$ and $j(b)$ itself is an image. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] applied to the ideal $bA$, $a\in bA$. Choose $r\in A$ with $a=br$. Then $x=a/b=r/1$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$.

source.place: Tag 033G, lemma-descent-normal, final principal-ideal contraction argument; Tag 05CK, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective

proof.text: Thus every element of $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ integral over $A$ belongs to $A$, so $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$ is an integrally closed domain. The prime $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary; [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] therefore says that $B$ is normal. If $B$ is the zero ring there are no prime ideals and this last assertion is vacuous; no step asserts that $B$ itself is a domain.

source.place: Tag 033G, lemma-descent-normal, conclusion; Tags 0309 and 00GV, definitions of normal domain and normal ring
